1.say: Never have I seen a first draft with this much evidence in it. Is that a compliment? Half of one. Not only did you find the figures, but you cited every source. And the other half? Rarely does a committee read forty pages. That much evidence they will never reach. So I cut it. You select. The strongest three claims stay. The rest go to an annex. Which three? Little did I expect to say this, but your problem is having too much. That I can live with.

grammar.label: inversion after negative and restrictive adverbials
grammar.form: Never / Rarely / Seldom / Not only / No sooner / Little + auxiliary + subject
grammar.meaning: strong emphasis on a negative or limiting idea

explanation.en: When a negative or restrictive adverbial opens the sentence, the subject and auxiliary swap places, exactly as in a question: 'Never have I seen anything like it.' If there is no auxiliary, 'do' supplies one: 'Rarely does he complain.'
explanation.uz: Gap boshida inkor yoki cheklov ma'noli ravish kelsa, ega bilan yordamchi fe'l o'rin almashadi — xuddi savoldagidek: 'Never have I seen anything like it.' Yordamchi fe'l bo'lmasa, 'do' qo'shiladi: 'Rarely does he complain.'

grammar.positive_example: Not only did the price rise, but the service got worse.
grammar.negative_example: Not only the price rose, but the service got worse.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida so'z tartibi bunday o'zgarmaydi, shuning uchun bu qurilma sun'iy tuyuladi; u yozma va rasmiy nutqning belgisi ekanini alohida tushuntirish kerak.

grammar.label: fronting for emphasis and cohesion
grammar.form: object / complement / adverbial moved to the front of the clause
grammar.meaning: puts the important or already-known element first

explanation.en: English normally puts the subject first, but any element can be fronted to link back to what came before: 'That I can accept. What I cannot accept is the delay.' Fronting a whole phrase does not invert the verb; only negative adverbials do that.
explanation.uz: Odatda ingliz tilida ega birinchi keladi, lekin oldingi gap bilan bog'lash uchun istalgan bo'lakni oldinga chiqarish mumkin: 'That I can accept. What I cannot accept is the delay.' Oddiy bo'lak oldinga chiqsa, fe'l o'rin almashmaydi — faqat inkor ravishlari bunga sabab bo'ladi.

grammar.positive_example: His first answer I could understand; his second I could not.
grammar.negative_example: His first answer could I understand; his second I could not.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida so'z tartibi erkin bo'lgani uchun oldinga chiqarish tabiiy tuyuladi, ammo ingliz tilida u kuchli uslubiy vosita — har gapda ishlatilmaydi.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Never have I seen a first draft with this much evidence in it.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Half of one. Not only did you find the figures, but you cited every source.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Rarely does a committee read forty pages. That much evidence they will never reach.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: You select. The strongest three claims stay. The rest go to an annex.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: The ones nobody can call unfounded. Anything you cannot substantiate, leave out.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The figure for staff I can prove. The cost of delay I cannot.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Then that figure leads. Little did I expect to say this, but your problem is having too much.
